newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian doctors threaten to quit over guard's attack.
newsitem.headline: Albanian doctors threaten to quit over guard's attack.

text.p: Doctors and nurses at Tirana's main military hospital threatened to resign on Monday unless President Sali Berisha identified the republican guards who opened fire on the hospital and terrorised its staff.
Some 500 hospital workers held a two-hour demonstration to protest at what they called the "unprecedented violation" of the hospital where hundreds of people are treated every day.
"Hands off the white uniforms, we are here for saving people", they shouted, while trade union leader Margarita Minai told reporters they would quit if authorities failed to stop the violence.
Sunday's attack underscored the lawlessness that has gripped the country since March when thousands of people rioted over the loss of their savings in fraudulent pyramid schemes.

Hospital sources said 50 to 60 guardsmen, in civilian clothes, attacked the hospital apparently seeking to avenge the death of a fellow guardsman who died of wounds suffered in a shootout last week in the central town of Cerrik.
"All the hospital staff tried to save him (the guardsman), but it was not possible," hospital director Ismail Kajo said.
"His head was severely wounded, he couldn't be saved," Health Minister Astrit Kalenja added.

Kajo said the guardsmen, driving two vans with official licence plates and two armoured personnel carriers opened fire on the hospital on Sunday morning before beating up his deputy and disarming military police protecting the hospital.
Bullet holes were left in the hospital's facade, though no injuries were reported. Staff and patients were scared and refused to respond to reporters questions.
"We ordered our police not to open fire, just to avoid a bloodshed, but we will not tolerate such banditry any more," Defence Minister Shaqir Vukaj said after visiting the hospital.
Vukaj said Prime Minister Bashkim Fino had called an urgent cabinet meeting before leaving for Italy and ordered officials to begin an investigation.
In a statement, the Council of Ministers said it viewed the event "as extremely grave and with unforeseen consequences".

"After hearing a report from the Commander of the Guard of the Republic, Prime Minister Bashkim Fino asked leading officials of the state's main institutions to publicly denounce this unprecedented incident," it said.
"The cabinet members expressed indignation and condemned Sunday's incident at the military hospital, considering it an unworthy and dangerous act for the Guard of the Republic," the statement added.
It said the government had demanded prosecution and punishment for the organisers "of this grave, shameful and dangerous event for Albanian democracy".
The guardsman who died at the hospital was wounded in a gunfight on Friday in Cerrik, about 70 kms (44 miles) from the capital Tirana, medical sources said.

Shooting also broke out on Sunday night at a police school in Tirana near the headquarters of the Italian-led multinational protection force. A military source said there were no reports of injuries and it was unclear if the shooting was targeted or was random firing in the air.
